title: Docs site offline edit & atomic commit playbook
author: Maya Thompson
body:
Overview
========
This playbook defines the recommended offline editing workflow and the atomic-commit policy for the Redwood docs site. It is intended for the developer experience (DevX) writers, SDK engineers, and contributor tooling owners who need to: prepare content without continuous connectivity, stage large curated snippet bundles, and guarantee atomic updates across the docs site, snippet-store, and snippet validation CI.

Motivation
----------
- Support contributors in low-bandwidth or intermittent network environments (device-only editing, airplane mode, secure sites).
- Prevent partial rollouts (e.g., docs update without required snippet or sample-code update) by enforcing atomic commits across multiple repositories and services.
- Reduce support escalations caused by broken snippets after a partial deploy.

Scope
-----
Applies to: docs authors, SDK sample owners, release engineers, and DX tooling maintainers.
Not in scope: runtime model-serving changes, infra-level network maintenance (see eng-infra runbooks).

Key concepts and definitions
----------------------------
- Offline edit bundle: a tarball or git bundle that contains content edits, snippet updates, and a manifest describing intended target branches.
- Atomic commit: a deploy step that ensures content + snippet-store + validation tags move from A->B together, or the operation aborts and rolls back.
- Snippet-store: the internal service that hosts canonical code snippets (internal URL: https://snippet-store.redwood.internal).
- Docs canary: a selective rollout to 2% of documentation traffic and the staging subdomain (docs-staging.redwood.com) before a full publish.

Goals and SLAs
--------------
- Docs site availability SLO for the main site: 99.95% (see eng-platform dashboards for exact monitoring).
- Deployment failure rate target: < 1% for atomic publish jobs.
- Mean time to recovery for broken snippets after an atomic publish: < 30 minutes with oncall involvement.

Offline edit workflow (recommended)
----------------------------------
1) Prepare local workspace
   - Clone the docs repo and snippet-store mirrors: git clone --mirror git@github.com:redwood/docs.git and git clone --mirror git@github.com:redwood/snippet-store.git
   - Create a working branch: git checkout -b offline/<your-issue-id>

2) Make edits locally
   - Update Markdown/Confluence-sourced files, add or modify snippets in snippet-store/src, update manifest.yaml (see manifest example below).
   - Run local validation: ./tools/local-docs-check --quiet. This runs lint, link-checker, and snippet extraction in offline mode.

3) Create an offline edit bundle
   - Generate a signed bundle: ./tools/mk-bundle --branch offline/<id> --author "Maya Thompson" --sign > offline-bundle-<id>.tar.gz
   - The bundle includes: docs patch, snippet-store patch, manifest.yaml, preflight-checks.json, and a GPG signature.

4) Transport bundle to a connected machine (trusted staging)
   - Use a secure transfer mechanism (scp to bastion or upload via private S3) and verify the bundle signature: gpg --verify offline-bundle-<id>.tar.gz.sig offline-bundle-<id>.tar.gz

5) Validate and submit to the atomic publish job
   - On the connected machine, extract and run: ./tools/verify-bundle offline-bundle-<id>.tar.gz
   - If verification passes, push to the release queue: ./tools/submit-atomic --bundle offline-bundle-<id>.tar.gz --target-branch release/<date>

Atomic commit policy
--------------------
- Atomic publish job responsibilities:
  - Orchestrate simultaneous PRs/patches across: docs repo, snippet-store, and devx-samples repository.
  - Trigger CI validation pipelines: docs-ci-lint, snippet-ci-tests, sample-integration-tests.
  - Create a single release tag (docs-release/<semver>) only if all checks pass.
  - Deploy to docs-staging and run canary checks.

- Rejection conditions (job will abort and rollback):
  - Any CI job fails (lint/link/snippet-compile/sample-build).
  - Canary validation fails (broken links, snippet mismatch, formatting regressions).
  - Manifest mismatch: required snippet versions not present in snippet-store.

- Rollback behavior:
  - The atomic job never merges individual PRs into production branches. It only merges when everything is green. On failure, it leaves feature branches intact for manual remediation and opens a triage issue with artifacts from the failed run.

Staging and release orchestration
---------------------------------
1) Canary publish (default):
   - Deploy release tag to docs-staging and to 2% of traffic via docs-proxy routing.
   - Run automated acceptance: link-checker, snippet-executor (executes code samples in a sandbox), readability metrics.
   - Notify #docs-canary Slack channel with failure/success summary.

2) Hold period:
   - Default hold: 2 hours for low-risk doc updates, 24 hours for sample or SDK surface changes.

3) Full publish:
   - If canary positive, the atomic job performs the merge to main and tags release. Content is then indexed by search and promoted to docs.redwood.com.

CI checks and snippet validation
--------------------------------
Required CI checks for atomic publish:
- docs-ci-lint (markdownlint + editorial style checks)
- docs-link-check (internal link validation across repos)
- snippet-ci-tests (compiles/runs language-specific snippets in ephemeral containers)
- sample-integration-tests (simple smoke tests that build sample apps)
- snippet-compat-check (ensures snippet versions match SDK version matrix)

Snippet validation details:
- Each snippet must include metadata header: language, runtime, expected-output, and snippet-id. Example header:

  <!-- snippet: id=auth-quickstart lang=python runtime=py3.10 expected-output=OK -->

- CI will reject snippets that: fail to compile/run, exceed runtime limits (120s for full-run tests), or assert outputs that differ from expected-output.

Manifest example (manifest.yaml)
--------------------------------
- purpose: tie docs edits to snippet versions and intended branches
- fields (text):
  - docs_branch: "offline/PR-1234"
  - snippet_store_branch: "offline/PR-1234-snippets"
  - sample_repo_branch: "offline/PR-1234-samples"
  - required_snippet_tags: ["sdk-python@2.3.1", "sdk-js@1.8.0"]
  - author: "Maya Thompson"
  - change_summary: "Update SDK quickstart and python auth snippet for new token flow"

(Refer to the appendix for a YAML example file.)

Rollback and emergency procedures
--------------------------------
- If a problematic publish reaches production: open an incident in PagerDuty with the tag "docs:broken-snippets" and notify #docs-oncall.
- The oncall will run the atomic rollback script: ./tools/atomic-rollback --tag <docs-release/tag> which will revert the release tag and re-deploy the previous release.
- Post-incident steps: create a postmortem in oncall/incidents/docs with timeline, root cause, and corrective actions.

Ownership and escalation
------------------------
- Primary owners:
  - DevX Docs (team alias: devx-docs@redwood.com) — content and editorial responsibility.
  - DevX Tooling (team alias: devx-tooling@redwood.com) — bundle tooling, verify-bundle, and atomic orchestrator.
  - SDK Samples (rotation): assigned sample owners in AUTHORS.md for language-specific snippets.
- Oncall escalation path:
  1) devx-oncall (PagerDuty)
  2) devx-tooling lead (pagerduty escalation rule)
  3) eng-platform (if infrastructure impacts observed)

Appendix: example commands and YAML
-----------------------------------
Sample offline bundle verification and submit: 

  # confirm GPG signature
  gpg --verify offline-bundle-123.sig offline-bundle-123.tar.gz

  # verify bundle contents and run staged checks
  ./tools/verify-bundle offline-bundle-123.tar.gz --run-ci-mock

  # submit for atomic publish (creates combined PRs and triggers CI)
  ./tools/submit-atomic --bundle offline-bundle-123.tar.gz --target-branch release/2026-02-03

Sample manifest.yaml (text):

  docs_branch: "offline/PR-1234"
  snippet_store_branch: "offline/PR-1234-snippets"
  sample_repo_branch: "offline/PR-1234-samples"
  required_snippet_tags:
    - "sdk-python@2.3.1"
    - "sdk-js@1.8.0"
  author: "Maya Thompson"
  change_summary: "Update quickstart for SDK auth changes"

FAQ (short)
-----------
Q: Can I push only docs without snippets?
A: Not under the atomic policy if the manifest declares snippet changes. For pure editorial updates, the atomic job allows docs-only bundles with an explicit no-snippet flag.

Q: What happens if snippet CI times out?
A: The atomic job marks the run as failed and opens a triage issue. For transient CI infra issues, re-run uses the same bundle artifacts.

Q: Where do I get help?
A: Ping #devx-docs in Slack for editorial questions and #devx-tooling for CI/tooling failures. For emergencies use devx-oncall.
